Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Phoenix AZ
110 AM MST Fri Feb 27 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Unseasonably strong high pressure will result in abnormally warm 
temperatures with afternoon highs approaching 20 degrees above 
normal. 

- Multiple daily record highs and overnight warm lows are likely to 
be tied or broken in Phoenix, Yuma, and El Centro through the 
weekend.
  
&&

.SHORT TERM /Today through Sunday/...
Little has changed in the past 24 hours with respect to the Conus 
flow pattern featuring pronounced ridging across the Southwest and 
flat troughing in the eastern United States. Objective analysis 
depicts a strengthening anti-cyclone center near the central Baja 
peninsula with H5 heights now closer to a 585-588dm range over the 
forecast area. Low level thermal profiles have responded with H8 
temperatures near +20C resulting in afternoon highs 15F-20F above 
normal. These synoptic measures are within the 99th percentile of 
late February climatology, and models are very consistent in showing 
little change over the next 48 hours. If anything, low level 
temperature will continue to warm; and narrow guidance spread yields 
unusually high confidence of widespread record highs through the 
weekend. By Sunday, the Conus pattern will begin to shift with 
Pacific energy starting to dampen midtropospheric heights, but not 
yet to the magnitude of significantly affecting boundary layer 
temperatures. 

&&

.LONG TERM /Monday through Thursday/... 
The first in a series of shortwaves will enter the western Conus 
during the first half of next week, though height falls will be 
somewhat gradual to arrive with sfc-H8 temperatures responding even 
slower. The trend among operational and ensemble members is now 
towards a more progressive and open wave propagating through 
northern Arizona introducing only modest and temporary height falls 
across the CWA. However, this evolution may be sufficient to incur 
gusty, downsloping sundowner winds in the typical wind prone areas 
of far SW Imperial County Monday evening. Otherwise, thermal 
profiles will only be depressed slightly with this more northern 
shortwave track, and guidance suggests temperatures only retreating 
to around 10F-15F above normal. This progression also reinforces the 
idea of poor moisture availability, and it would be surprising if 
any location in the state received precipitation. However, it still 
appears this wave will carve out a void in the midlevel flow pattern 
encouraging trailing shortwave energy to establish mean negative 
height anomalies over the Great Basin, and eventually increased 
precipitation chances, albeit beyond the temporal scope of this 
forecast package. 

&&

.AVIATION...Updated at 0515Z. 

South Central Arizona including KPHX, KIWA, KSDL, and KDVT: 
No aviation weather concerns will exist through Friday evening under 
periods of FEW-SCT high cirrus cloud decks. The overall wind pattern 
will exhibit diurnal tendencies with periods of light variability. 
Speeds will generally remain under 10 kts. 


Southeast California/Southwest Arizona including KIPL and KBLH: 
No major aviation weather concerns will exist through the next 24 
hours under FEW to at times SCT high cirrus decks. Winds at both 
terminals will be out of the W/NW. Speeds at KIPL will aob 7 kt.
Whereas at KBLH, wind speeds will generally be aob 10, with some 
occasional gusts into the mid teens possible during the afternoon 
and early evening hours. 

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Warm and dry weather will continue through the middle of next week 
as well above normal temperatures cool slightly as the weather 
pattern begins to shift. Minimum afternoon humidity levels will fall 
into the teens across the lower elevations with some areas nearing 
single digits Sunday and Monday. Humidity levels will only be 
somewhat higher in foothills and mountains. This will follow mostly 
fair to good overnight recovery of 30-60% though some areas of poor 
recovery under 20% will exist early next week. Wind speeds will 
largely remain under 15 mph with modest afternoon upslope gusts 15-
25 mph becoming common. The strongest gusts would be expected Monday 
and Thursday afternoon. Overall conditions will be favorable for 
early spring prescribed burning operations. 

&&
